questions.question: VNet1 is peered with VNet2. VNet2 is peered with VNet3. No other peerings or routes exist. Which statement is true?

options.text: Virtual machines in VNet1 cannot communicate with virtual machines in VNet3.
options.why: Correct. Virtual network peering is not transitive.

options.text: Virtual machines in VNet1 can communicate with virtual machines in VNet3 through VNet2.
options.why: Peering is not transitive, so VNet2 does not forward traffic between its peers without additional configuration.

options.text: VNet1 and VNet3 can communicate only if they are in the same region.
options.why: Region does not change the behavior. Peering is not transitive in any region.

options.text: VNet1 and VNet3 can communicate if the peerings use the Allow virtual network access setting.
options.why: That setting allows traffic between the two peered networks only.

questions.explanation: To connect VNet1 and VNet3, peer them directly or route traffic through a network virtual appliance in VNet2 by using user-defined routes.

questions.question: You create a peering from VNet1 to VNet2. The peering status shows Initiated. What should you do?

options.text: Create a peering from VNet2 to VNet1
options.why: Correct. A peering requires a link from each virtual network before it shows Connected.

options.text: Enable gateway transit on the peering
options.why: Gateway transit shares a gateway. It does not complete the peering.

options.text: Restart the virtual machines in both virtual networks
options.why: Restarting VMs does not change the peering status.

options.text: Add a route table to both virtual networks
options.why: Routes are not required for a peering to connect.

questions.explanation: The status changes to Connected when both peering links exist.

questions.question: A hub virtual network contains a VPN gateway that connects to the on-premises network. A spoke virtual network is peered with the hub. Resources in the spoke must reach the on-premises network through the hub gateway. Which two settings should you configure? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Allow gateway transit on the hub peering to the spoke
options.why: Correct. The virtual network that has the gateway allows peers to use it.

options.text: Use remote gateways on the spoke peering to the hub
options.why: Correct. The spoke uses the gateway in the remote hub.

options.text: Use remote gateways on the hub peering to the spoke
options.why: The hub has its own gateway and does not use a remote gateway.

options.text: Deploy a second VPN gateway in the spoke
options.why: A spoke that uses remote gateways cannot have its own gateway.

questions.explanation: Gateway transit requires Allow gateway transit on the side that has the gateway and Use remote gateways on the side that does not.

questions.question: You attempt to create a peering between VNet1 (10.0.0.0/16) and VNet2 (10.0.128.0/17). The operation fails. What is the cause?

options.text: The address spaces of the virtual networks overlap.
The virtual networks are in different resource groups.
options.why: Peering is supported across resource groups, subscriptions and tenants.

options.text: Gateway transit is not enabled.
options.why: Gateway transit is optional and does not affect whether a peering can be created.

options.text: The virtual networks use different DNS servers.
options.why: DNS settings do not prevent peering.

questions.explanation: Virtual networks with overlapping address spaces cannot be peered.

questions.question: A network virtual appliance (NVA) in a hub virtual network forwards traffic from Spoke1 to Spoke2. Spoke2 drops the forwarded traffic. Routes and IP forwarding are configured correctly. What should you configure?

options.text: Allow forwarded traffic on the Spoke2 peering to the hub
options.why: Correct. This setting accepts traffic that did not originate in the hub.

options.text: Use remote gateways on the Spoke2 peering
options.why: This setting shares a VPN gateway. It does not accept forwarded traffic.

options.text: Allow gateway transit on the Spoke1 peering
options.why: Gateway transit is set on the virtual network that has the gateway.

options.text: A service endpoint on the Spoke2 subnet
options.why: Service endpoints apply to Azure PaaS services, not traffic between virtual networks.

questions.explanation: Traffic that an NVA forwards did not originate in the hub, so the receiving peering must allow forwarded traffic.
